name: personal identity number
note: Latvia's sheet (its government's own sheet on the OECD's automatic-exchange portal ('Information on Tax Identification Numbers'; the OECD's index page sits behind a bot check and wasn't opened, the sheet itself came straight back)), read 2026-10-30: an individual's TIN is identical with the personal identity number; since 1 July 2017 every person newly entered in the Register of Natural Persons gets an 11-digit number starting with 3, a random second digit from 2 to 9 and nine random digits (older numbers carry the birth date, not modelled). The sheet names the Register, not the office keeping it. Read as given on registration, to residents. No check rule, fee or time is stated.

sources.title: OECD AEOI portal, Latvia: Information on Tax Identification Numbers (the jurisdiction's own sheet)
sources.said: TIN issued to individuals are identical with their personal identity number. 1) As of 1 July 2017 an individual personal identity number, starting with the digit “3” will be allocated to all persons, regarding whom information will be included in the Register of Natural Persons (initial registration of a person). ... The first digit of the personal identity number shall be “3”, the second digit is a random digit between "2" and "9" automatically generated by the system
